tier_reason: The README Benchmark section shows two wrk runs (nginx on port 80: 161390.39 req/s, 3.54 ms avg latency; libuhttpd on port 8080: 281328.83 req/s, 2.12 ms), so the 1.74x ratio (derived from page data) is correct. These are first-party numbers with no benchmark script, no compiler or flags, no CPU, no nginx version or configuration, which is tier C.

corrections.caveats: README only (Benchmark section, undated; current release 3.14.2); no compiler, flags, CPU, kernel, nginx version or nginx configuration (worker_processes, access logging, sendfile) stated, so tier C. The bundled example/simple_server.c is a single libev event loop serving files from a docroot; the README does not say which server binary or how many processes libuhttpd used, nor how many nginx workers ran. Response sizes differ: wrk reports binary units, so nginx read 385.09 MB for 1,622,012 requests (about 249 bytes each) and libuhttpd 547.18 MB for 2,826,394 requests (about 203 bytes each); the servers returned different headers, so the comparison is not like for like. Single 10 s run on localhost with client and server sharing the machine, no repeats; test.html is not described. Last commit is a CMake 4 compatibility fix merged 2025-08-08.

notes: Numbers and metadata check out (MIT, 432 stars, 75 forks, not a fork, last commit 2025-08-08, so stale). Shortcomings to record: first-party single wrk run with unknown nginx configuration and worker count, different response header sizes (about 249 vs 203 bytes per response), no build or hardware details.

tier_reason: The uWebSockets README table rates libwebsockets 2.0 and WebSocket++ v0.7.0 against uWS in the same harness (11x vs 63x lighter, equal vs 4x connection rate, 6x vs 3x short messages, 4x vs 2x huge messages), so the libwebsockets-vs-WebSocket++ ratios exist only as derived cross-ratios of rounded integers. Benchmark code is public (benchmarks/lws.cpp, wsPP.cpp, scalability.cpp, throughput.cpp, Makefile with g++ -std=c++11 -O3) but no CPU, compiler version or libwebsockets build is stated, so not A; a competitor's table, not an independent suite, so C.

corrections.caveats: The numbers are a competitor's table: the uWebSockets README in iCyberon/uWebSockets, a 0-star fork snapshot of uNetworking/uWebSockets whose last commit is v0.6.3 on 2016-06-26 (upstream no longer carries the table). libwebsockets and WebSocket++ are never compared directly; every ratio is a rounded integer relative to uWS, so the derived figures (about 5.7x lighter than WebSocket++, about 4x faster connection setup, about 2x slower on short- and huge-message echo) are rough. Benchmark code is in benchmarks/ (lws.cpp, wsPP.cpp, scalability.cpp, throughput.cpp; Makefile uses -O3 and links the system /usr/lib/libwebsockets.a with the libev backend); the libwebsockets echo server was written by the uWS author with a uWS-style thin message queue, and the memory test used 500k connections for libwebsockets and WebSocket++ versus 1M for uWS. No CPU, compiler version or kernel stated; libwebsockets 2.0 (2016) and WebSocket++ 0.7.0 are old versions. benchmarks/README.md notes that with one frame per send the WebSocket++-to-uWS gap shrinks from 3x to 2x. Against the category's listed baseline uWebSockets, libwebsockets loses on every row (11x more memory, equal connection rate, 6x slower short messages, 4x slower huge messages); WebSocket++ is not a listed baseline for websocket-grpc-rpc. The current libwebsockets README makes no benchmark claims. License is MIT with some files under BSD-2/BSD-3, zlib, Apache-2.0 (mbedtls wrapper, built only with mbedtls) and OFL, and test apps and minimal examples under CC0.

notes: Table numbers match the page and the record already labels its cross-ratios as derived; metadata checks out (MIT, 5.3k stars, last commit 2026-10-06, active). Shortcomings to record: evidence is a 2016 competitor table with no direct libwebsockets-vs-WebSocket++ run, win only on memory and connection setup while message throughput is about 2x worse, slower than uWebSockets (a listed baseline) on every row, baseline_in_list corrected to false. Low confidence entry; keep at C.
